The region shown above enclosed by the curves $y=\sqrt{x}+1$ and $y=\frac{x}{2}+1$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=-1.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x}+1 & =\frac{x}{2}+1 \\ \sqrt{x} & =\frac{x}{2} \\ 2\sqrt{x} & =x \\ x & =0,4\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=4.$

Now, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/7ce02bca7667a9c32971b7840ff2ba4b96ef3a5c9b18aceaeb5b9b713cc7b36f.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=\frac{x}{2}+1,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}+1.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/6cb557a57a189a426b6cccacd599562332b05aace5bbbfc5d996b0d53fed3359.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}[\,(\sqrt{x}+1)-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{[\sqrt{x}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=\frac{x}{2}+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/26886afd61251cae273c086dba59dcfa912665cdb788b0c3ef866bf61907efa2.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}[\,(\frac{x}{2}+1)-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{[\frac{x}{2}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{[\sqrt{x}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{[\frac{x}{2}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}({(\sqrt{x}+2)}^{2}-{(\frac{x}{2}+2)}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}(-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-x+4\sqrt{x})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(-\frac{1}{12}\,{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}+\frac{8}{3}\,{x}^{3/2})|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\pi ((-\frac{1}{12}\,(4)^{3}-\frac{1}{2}\,(4)^{2}+\frac{8}{3}\,(4)^{3/2})-(0)) \\  & =\pi (8) \\  & =8\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
